sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: import it in code, then go mod tidy (or go get package@version). tidy scans imports, adds missing requires, removes unused ones, and updates go.sum.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The workflow, executed:

```bash
# 1. Import in code
import "github.com/google/uuid"

# 2. Either: let tidy find it
go mod tidy
# (adds require github.com/google/uuid v1.6.0 — verified)

# Or: get a specific version
go get github.com/google/uuid@v1.6.0
go get github.com/google/uuid@latest

# 3. Run
go run main.go
```

The tidy contract: go mod tidy is the reflex — it scans the code's imports, reconciles the requires list (add what's imported, remove what isn't), downloads, and writes both go.mod and go.sum. The output: a go.mod that exactly reflects the code.

The go get variants:
go get pkg@latest — the latest tagged release
go get pkg@v1.2.3 — a specific version
go get pkg@branch-name — a branch (for testing upstream changes)
go get -u ./... — upgrade all direct dependencies
go get pkg@none — REMOVE a dependency

The upgrade path: -u updates to the newest MINOR/PATCH; @major upgrades need explicit version (v2 module paths end in /v2 — semantic import versioning).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I[import in code] --> T[go mod tidy]
    T --> S[scan imports]
    S --> M[add missing to go.mod]
    M --> D[download + verify]
    D --> G[go.sum updated]
    T --> R[remove unused]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The resolution pipeline: the import path in code → checked against go.mod's requires → if missing, the module at the path's prefix is fetched (the longest matching module), version resolved via MVS, downloaded to the module cache (verified against go.sum), and added to go.mod.

The major-version suffixing: semantic import versioning requires v2+ modules to have /v2 in their path — github.com/pkg/dep/v2. A v2 import and a v1 import are DIFFERENT modules (both can coexist in the same build — the migration path for breaking changes).

The replace directive: go mod edit -replace github.com/pkg=/local/path — points a module at a local checkout for development. The canonical workflow: replace the dependency locally, test the fix, upstream it, remove the replace. The replace lives in go.mod but SHOULD NOT be committed for non-development reasons.
